comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
**Done.** `increase_font_size`, `decrease_font_size` and `reset_font_size` are ordinary actions - in `Action::ALL`, rebindable through `[keymap]`, and menu items under View.

The card left two things open; both are decided.

**Per window, not per pane.** Ghostty sizes each surface separately and Muster does not, which is the deliberate difference: the claim is a grid you read at a glance, and one with ragged cell sizes is harder to read. A pane made *after* a resize gets the size in force, so a split does not open at the configured size beside four panes somebody had grown.

**Remembered**, under `[window]` in `window.toml` beside the sidebar flag.

**What is stored is an offset in points, not a size**, and that is the part worth knowing. Muster does not know the size it is offsetting from: `[font] size` is optional, and when it is absent the number is libghostty's and never crosses back over the seam. An offset survives not knowing that, and it is also what a chord means - one point bigger than whatever you had. `cmd+0` sets it to zero, which is the only way back out of a size somebody has pressed themselves into.

**Chords are `cmd+=`, `cmd+-`, `cmd+0`**, and they are the one place Muster deliberately does not copy Ghostty's binding. Ghostty binds both `cmd+plus` and `cmd+equal` because an action there can carry several chords; Muster gives each action one, so it has to pick, and the one to give is the key a hand actually presses.

Two things worth carrying forward:

- **The renderer actions are driven by string and nothing in the suite can validate the names.** `ghostty_surface_binding_action` needs a live surface, so a GPU and a window. `ghostty_config_trigger` looked like a way to parse-check them and is not - it answers tag 0 for a real action and a nonsense one alike, so a test built on it asserted nothing and was deleted. What replaced it: the call's return value is no longer discarded, and a refusal logs `renderer.action.refused` naming the action. A pin bump that renames one shows up as a log line rather than as a chord that quietly does nothing.
- **Idempotence is not free.** libghostty's font-size actions are relative, so the shell resets before applying an offset - the core republishes the whole presentation on every change and a new pane is handed the offset in force, so the same number arrives more than once as a matter of course.

Verified in a real window: a saved offset of 5 comes back on the next launch, reaches the shell, and is carried out on a live surface with no refusal.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`cmd+plus` and `cmd+minus` are reflexes in every terminal and Muster has neither. `config.font_size = 0` inherits the configured size once at surface creation (`Renderer.swift`), so the only way to change it is to edit a config and relaunch.

Worth noting this is a Muster *action* rather than an appearance setting, so it is wanted whatever happens to the appearance loan (see the appearance card): it joins `Action::ALL`, becomes rebindable and gets a menu item, like every other action.

Two things to work out: whether the size is per-window or per-pane (Ghostty does per-surface), and whether a changed size is remembered - it is presentation state, so `[window]` in the state file is the obvious home now that one exists.
title: 🔍 Font size is fixed for the life of a launch
